city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.lede: Yesterday's high of 43°F was the 27th coolest November 13 high (tied) of 143 since 1872, the coolest since 2022.
text.p_yest: The high of 43°F was the 27th coolest November 13 high (tied) of 143 since 1872, the coolest since 2022. The normal high for the date is 55°F, and the record is 78°F (1955). The low of 37°F was typical for November 13.
text.t_rec: Lexington has nearly stopped setting record lows
text.p_rec: If Lexington's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Lexington has set 33 standing record lows, far fewer than the 69 that chance alone would give, and 83 record highs, close to the 69 that chance alone would give. The 1930s hold the most record highs of any decade (73). Lexington's all-time high is 108°F, on July 10, 1936.
text.t_chg: Lexington's nights have warmed since 1986. Its days have warmed.
text.p_chg: Across 141 complete years: Lexington's average low shows no clear change: +0.03°F per decade, a range (−0.03 to +0.08) that includes zero. Lexington's average high has risen +0.18°F per decade (95% range +0.11 to +0.24), about +2.7°F since 1873. The last 40 years tell a different story: since 1986, lows have risen +0.49°F per decade (95% range +0.15 to +0.82) and highs have risen +0.66°F per decade (95% range +0.24 to +1.08). The full record joins different observing sites over the years, and a move (for example, from the city to a cooler airport) can hide or exaggerate a long-run trend, so the recent decades are the clearer guide here.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in none. Highs rose in 9 of 12 months.
text.p_rain: Lexington's yearly precipitation has risen +0.65 inches per decade (95% range +0.32 to +0.97), about +9.8 inches since 1873. The 1991–2020 normal is 49.8 inches a year. The wettest year was 2018 (71.98 in); the driest, 1930 (24.89 in).
